sourceEvidence.label: Retained Ollama connection attribution source review

assessment.summary: The read-only attached preflight can be narrowed to one retained HTTP/1 connection with point-in-time kernel attribution, while remaining inert and unqualified.

nonNegotiables: The endpoint remains an explicit HTTP IP-literal loopback address.
The operation performs no generation, acquisition, activation, or runtime lifecycle mutation.
No transport failure may trigger an implicit retry or reconnect.
Windows evidence is described as a context-binding PID, not exclusive socket ownership.
Linux evidence requires exactly one visible same-UID holder under the current proc, PID namespace, and network namespace policy and fails closed on observed permission or enumeration gaps.
macOS attached response attribution remains unsupported without a reviewed public mechanism.
The report remains inert with qualified set to false.
Errors and traces remain content-free and path-free.
assumptions: No measured latency, memory, or owner-observation budget was supplied.
Other authorized local processes and malicious administrators remain outside the repository threat model.
Point-in-time snapshots cannot prove continuous exclusive ownership or application-handler execution.

opportunities.title: Bind read-only preflight traffic to one retained connection
opportunities.summary: Replace opaque pooled transport for attached preflight with one direct HTTP/1 session whose reverse 4-tuple receives bounded kernel attribution before traffic and after every response.
opportunities.diagnosis: The process witness brackets an HTTP preflight whose pooled client does not expose the selected TCP connection, so listener stability cannot be promoted into response attribution.

evidence.claim: The adapter sends requests through a reusable reqwest client and does not expose the selected connection.
One preflight performs several ordered HTTP requests without a connection lease.
The bracketed report explicitly records response_bound and qualified as false.
Windows listener observation uses an owner-PID table and retained process handle.
Linux listener observation maps a socket inode to visible descriptor owners and retains a pidfd.
macOS attached-process observation is intentionally unsupported.
The existing listener witness vocabulary can be extended with a distinct connection-attribution lease without granting authority.
The existing proposed decision reserves one persistent HTTP connection and exact 4-tuple attribution as follow-up work.

desiredInvariants: One attached preflight opens exactly one direct TCP connection and performs exactly one HTTP/1 handshake.
Every request and response in the operation uses that retained client socket object.
The reverse established 4-tuple has the same admissible kernel-attributed process instance before application traffic and after every complete response.
A missing, closed, ambiguous, incomplete, or changed connection observation terminates the operation without reconnecting.
The listener, process, executable, runtime, inventory, model details, and residency remain stable through the final observation.
Successful evidence remains point-in-time, inert, response-limited, and unqualified.

options.title: Keep pooled reqwest with listener snapshots
options.summary: Retain the current client and add more listener observations around opaque requests.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The pool still selects connections invisibly and may reconnect after a close.
More listener snapshots narrow drift windows but do not identify the connection carrying a response.
The report must continue to state response_bound false and qualified false.
Windows process drift remains observable, but connection ownership is not established.
Linux listener drift remains observable, but no accepted connection inode is selected.
macOS remains unsupported.
No connection-attribution vocabulary or lease is introduced.
The persistent-connection follow-up remains incomplete.

tradeoffs.assessment: Additional snapshots reduce the interval in which listener drift can remain unnoticed, but they cannot attribute a response to a selected connection.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run listener-replacement and server-close fixtures and confirm that successful responses can still cross different pooled connections.

tradeoffs.assessment: The existing connection pool and request path remain unchanged; added listener snapshots add platform observation cost.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure preflight wall time and kernel-observation time for one and eight target models.

tradeoffs.assessment: The client pool and bounded response buffers remain; each added snapshot temporarily allocates its existing bounded platform buffer.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak resident memory for one and eight target preflights.

tradeoffs.assessment: More drift checks can reject unstable runtimes, while reqwest can still recover transport availability through an opaque new connection.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise graceful close, reset, idle expiry, and listener replacement without wall-clock sleeps.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new transport subsystem appears, but snapshot failures still cannot explain which connection carried a response.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review stable reason codes produced by every platform fixture.

tradeoffs.assessment: The public preflight shape and adapter transport remain compatible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run existing preflight process and serialization tests unchanged.

residualRisks: A response can arrive over a connection that was never attributed.
The pool can reconnect between snapshots.
Listener ownership does not identify an accepted socket or handler.

workPackages: Add listener reobservation after each opaque request group.
acceptanceCriteria: The report continues to set response_bound and qualified to false.
migrationNotes: This option preserves the current transport but does not complete retained response attribution.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove the additional snapshots and retain the current bracket.

options.title: Use one retained HTTP/1 session with kernel attribution
options.summary: Create a direct loopback TCP connection, retain it for all ordered preflight requests, and attribute its reverse established 4-tuple before traffic and after every response.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The attached preflight bypasses the opaque pool and owns one direct session.
Every ordered request is serialized on one retained sender and fully drained before the next.
The report can record bounded response attribution but remains inert and qualified false because snapshots are not exclusive proof.
Windows can bind the connection row to a context PID and retained process instance, not prove exclusive handle ownership.

Linux can require exactly one visible same-UID holder under the current proc and namespace policy and fail closed on observed permission or enumeration gaps, but cannot prove that no invisible holder exists.
macOS remains explicitly unsupported for attached response attribution.
A separate bounded connection lease and redacted reason taxonomy extend the safe facade.
The selected option implements the reserved persistent-connection follow-up without overstating its strength.

tradeoffs.assessment: The client socket becomes an owned capability and implicit reconnects become impossible; point-in-time platform attribution still cannot prove exclusive accepted-socket ownership or handler execution.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use retry-canary, owner-change, descriptor-handoff, proxy, and listener-replacement fixtures with exact stable failure reasons.

tradeoffs.assessment: Per-response kernel attribution adds table or descriptor scans, while one retained connection avoids repeated handshakes during an operation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark one and eight models, record total time, per-response owner-check time, and request throughput against the pooled baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: The operation retains one socket, one HTTP driver, one process lease, and bounded observer buffers; it removes no existing response buffering.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak resident memory and maximum aggregate buffered response bytes for one and eight models.

tradeoffs.assessment: A server close, owner-view gap, or connection-state transition becomes a terminal failure instead of an opportunity to reconnect, producing deterministic evidence at the cost of availability.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run graceful close, FIN, reset, idle expiry, permission denial, and observation-deadline cases under paused time.

tradeoffs.assessment: The project owns a small transport and a new platform connection observer with more diagnostic stages and native CI obligations.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit error-code coverage, native fixture stability, redaction, and platform unsupported behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: The attached preflight gains a dedicated session path and connection witness while ordinary discovery and generation remain on reqwest until separately reviewed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run old and new preflight schemas side by side, preserve existing v1 decoding, and compare canonical reports.

residualRisks: Windows exposes a context-binding PID rather than an exclusive set of accepted-socket holders.
Linux attribution names exactly one visible same-UID holder under the current proc and namespace policy but cannot exclude invisible holders.
Snapshots can miss transient handoff between observations.
The immediate peer can proxy to another process or remote service.
Connection attribution does not prove which application handler generated response bytes.

workPackages: Define the retained-session and connection-attribution contracts.
Implement one direct bounded HTTP/1 preflight session without a reconnect path.
Add Windows context-PID and Linux conditional holder attribution for the reverse established 4-tuple.
Join response checks to the existing listener and executable witness.
Add deterministic transport, platform, redaction, cancellation, and resource tests.
acceptanceCriteria: One preflight performs exactly one TCP connect and one HTTP handshake.
Every request uses the retained socket and no failure reaches a second listener.
The reverse 4-tuple attribution matches the retained process before traffic and after every complete response, subject to the explicit platform evidence scope.
Any close, absence, ambiguity, incomplete view, drift, cancellation, or deadline fails closed.
The report remains inert and qualified false.
migrationNotes: Keep the existing pooled adapter for non-attached operations during the first slice.
Version the new response-attribution evidence without reinterpreting prior reports.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the new attached response-attribution command path and retain the published listener-witness preflight with response_bound false.

options.title: Move to a managed runtime chain
options.summary: Verify and launch the runtime under application-owned lifecycle, package, listener, process, and retained-connection capabilities.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The managed chain can own its connection transport rather than use an opaque shared pool.
The operation can retain lifecycle and transport capabilities across all requests.
Managed ownership strengthens process evidence, but qualification still requires package, isolation, and evaluation closure.
A child process handle supplies stronger process identity, though Windows socket duplication remains a separate fact.
A retained child and known listener creation reduce dependence on system-wide proc ownership enumeration.
Managed launch can supply process identity on macOS, but accepted-connection attribution still needs a supported design.
Managed lifecycle requires distinct capability contracts rather than attached witness reinterpretation.
The persistent connection becomes one part of a larger managed package and isolation chain.

tradeoffs.assessment: Application-owned package, launch, lifetime, listener, and connection capabilities reduce ambient attachment ambiguity; handler execution and proxy exclusion still require explicit mechanisms.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model launch inheritance, package replacement, child escape, socket passing, proxying, and shutdown recovery before implementation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Managed startup, package verification, readiness, and shutdown add work outside the request loop; a retained process may improve repeated-operation latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure cold start, warm operation, idle residency, and shutdown across supported platforms and hardware classes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Retaining a managed runtime consumes model and process memory for a policy-defined lifetime.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak and idle resident memory under one-operation and repeated-operation policies.

tradeoffs.assessment: Lifecycle ownership makes restart and cleanup explicit but introduces child supervision, readiness, crash recovery, and update coordination.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run crash, hung startup, partial update, locked executable, orphan, and interrupted shutdown fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: The product becomes responsible for installation boundaries, launch policy, logs, resource policy, upgrades, and support across platforms.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Define support, diagnostics, recovery, update, and uninstallation runbooks before selecting this option.

tradeoffs.assessment: This changes the user-managed runtime constraint and depends on package-manifest and isolation milestones not yet complete.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype as a separate managed mode while retaining attached observation as an explicit compatibility path.

residualRisks: Managed launch does not by itself prove which handler produced a response.
Socket inheritance and child helper topology need explicit policy.
Package, effective configuration, and network isolation evidence remain separate prerequisites.
The option materially expands product lifecycle authority.

workPackages: Complete package-manifest and isolation design before runtime management.
Define child lifecycle, readiness, connection, recovery, and update capabilities.
Implement a separate managed mode without reinterpreting attached evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: The application retains package, process, listener, and connection capabilities for the complete operation.
Crash recovery and shutdown leave no ambiguous runtime authority.
Qualification remains blocked until package, isolation, and evaluation evidence pass.
migrationNotes: Reserve this option for the later managed-runtime milestone.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Keep managed mode separately selectable and return users to the inert attached preflight without migrating authority records.

opportunities.recommendation: Select one retained HTTP/1 session for the next read-only slice. It closes implicit reconnect ambiguity at proportionate scope while preserving explicit platform limitations and qualified false.

openQuestions: What owner-observation latency budget is acceptable after each response?
Should the first retained-session implementation support IPv6 and IPv4 together or ship them behind separate native fixtures?
Can Windows expose a stronger supported accepted-socket identity than a context-binding PID without expanding privilege?
Which proc visibility profiles will be supported on Linux?
What public mechanism, if any, would justify macOS attached response attribution?
